policyReasoning: ssl.create_default_context with SERVER_AUTH constructs SSLContext(PROTOCOL_TLS_CLIENT), sets CERT_REQUIRED and check_hostname=True, and loads the supplied certificate trust material.

The actual Python 3.12.14/OpenSSL 3.5.8 context has minimum_version TLSv1_2 (771). Version-range enforcement rejects TLSv1 and TLSv1_1 independently of whether deprecated OP_NO_TLSv1/OP_NO_TLSv1_1 option bits are set.
Both direct default-context and h2-ALPN variants retain the same TLS version range and verification policy.

A read-only scan of both Task-07 test directories found no assignments lowering minimum_version/maximum_version, disabling verify_mode/check_hostname, monkey-patching ssl functions, or using unverified/legacy-version contexts.
The raw PR comments are preserved as observed messages; their existence does not establish the current remote code-scanning alert state or a failed required check.
limits: The probe inspects actual SSLContext policy in memory with socket audit events forbidden; it does not claim a negotiated network TLS version.
No support claim is made for older Python runtimes or a different SSL build. Their default context policy would require separate evidence if they became an execution target.

The first metadata-only probe attempt discovered that this runtime embeds _ssl as a built-in module with no __file__; it emitted no JSON. The probe now records origin=built-in rather than fabricating an extension path or hash.
No remote CodeQL alert was modified or dismissed; the parent must follow ordinary required-check/review rules.
